description:
The death of a worker at a Russian plague research centre in Siberia has raised concerns that the deadly disease could spread.

The World Health Organisation and the United States have both asked Russia for more information on the circumstances surrounding the incident.   US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has urged Russia to release more information.  "I think it's incumbent upon Russia to obviously share more information with the world," Rubio told reporters. "We're watching it very closely, hour by hour."

The incident has sparked a flurry of speculation about the circumstances in which the 28-year-old woman died. Russian officials have said they are still investigating the cause of the death but those who came into contact with the victim all tested negative to pneumonic plague.

Reports first emerged on Friday of almost 200 people being placed under observation in Siberia's Irkutsk region following the death.

author: BBC News
description:
US death row inmate Christa Pike is conscious and speaking, after surviving a failed execution attempt in the US state of Tennessee, her lawyers have said.

Pike, 50, continues to receive critical medical care while handcuffed in hospital, according to the statement from her attorneys.

She was sentenced to death following her conviction for murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995. But Pike survived two lethal injections and was transferred to a hospital in Nashville for treatment.

Her lawyers had said in the days afterwards that she was unconscious while medical staff cleared her body of the pentobarbital injected during the execution attempt. It was suggested that she might have suffered irreversible brain damage.

Pike's lawyers said that her recovery is "medically unprecedented", and while her prognosis remains unclear, "at a minimum, we expect a long recovery".

title: US death row inmate Christa Pike “conscious and talking” after surviving lethal injection | BBC News

At a recent Meta product launch, Mark Zuckerberg promised that the company’s smart glasses would give wearers “new superpowers”, but what are they?

description:
The number of children involved in care proceedings before they reach their first birthdays is at a persistently high level across England, according to experts who have published new figures.

Data from the universities of Lancaster and Oxford indicates care proceedings for babies have risen by 64% over the past two decades, with one in 118 infants affected. The figures - up to 2024-25 - peaked during Covid, before dropping slightly and plateauing.

While there are cases where it is unsafe for parents to continue contact with their children, experts have told File on 4 Investigates that many babies may not have needed to go into care if support had been in place.

And, since very young children who go into care are more likely to be adopted than older children, there are also concerns from experts that some may have been permanently separated from their birth families unnecessarily.
